newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea announces arrest of U.S. spy.
newsitem.headline: North Korea announces arrest of U.S. spy.

text.p: Isolated North Korea announced on Sunday that it had arrested a U.S. citizen in August as a spy working for rival South Korea.
The official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said Evan Carl Hunzike was arrested on August 24 inside North Korea after he crossed the Amnok River.
KCNA did not say why it took more than a month to announce the arrest and did not provide further details of the man, other than to say he worked for South Korean intelligence.

"On August 24, a public security organ of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea arrested a U.S. citizen, Evan Carl Hunzike, when he illegally entered the DPRK, crossing the Amnok River," KCNA said in a communique seen in Tokyo.
Amnok River runs on North Korea's border with China.
"He admitted that he is a U.S. citizen and that he illegally entered the DPRK for the purpose of getting information on its domestic situation," KCNA said.

"It has been proved by investigation that he was sent for espionage by South Korea's agency for National Security Planning. He will have to take appropriate penal responsibility under the DPRK criminal law," the agency said in the short communique.
The report follows a heated row between the two arch-foes over a North Korean submarine which ran aground on the coast of South Korea last month.
On Saturday, North Korea threatened retaliation over the incident.

"Our retaliation will be merciless," KCNA said in a dispatch on Saturday. "Blood should be paid for (with) blood," the agency said in the most harshly-worded threat so far over the submarine incident.
Of the 26 North Koreans who landed on an east coast beach last month, 22 have been killed by Southern troops or found dead, one has been captured alive and a hunt is on for three others.
Pyongyang has demanded the return of the submarine, found grounded on rocks on September 18, as well as the survivors and the bodies of the dead crew.
South Korean newspapers on Sunday said Seoul would freeze economic exchanges with North Korea after Pyongyang's threats.
